The resolutions were reached at the association’s general assembly, its highest decision-making organ, held in Abuja under the leadership of its national president, Bello Lawal. In a statement, ALGON said the amendments were adopted through a resolution supported by an absolute majority of members, following deliberations by the National Executive Council (NEC) on constitutional provisions affecting the association’s operations.
The assembly also considered and adopted reports on projects, programmes and activities undertaken since its last general assembly in March 2021. It reviewed challenges affecting the association’s functionality and resolved to align its operations with contemporary governance realities. As part of efforts to strengthen its institutional framework, the assembly resolved to reconstitute the Board of Trustees to fill vacancies created by the deaths of some members, in accordance with the association’s constitution.
It also emphasised the need for local governments to build institutional capacity, improve administrative efficiency and strengthen their position within Nigeria’s governance structure.
The assembly approved a change to the designation of the association’s administrative head from secretary-general to director-general. It also considered and approved the association’s annual budgets prior to implementation, along with reports from principal officers and other matters of strategic importance.
ALGON said the NEC, constitutionally responsible for managing the association, had prepared and presented annual financial statements and budget proposals through its secretariat, including recommendations on standing orders and rules of procedure.
The meeting attracted representatives from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, including local government chairmen, councillors, vice-chairmen, members of the Board of Trustees, development partners, consultants and civil society organisations.
A major highlight was the attendance of Imo State governor and Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum, Senator Hope Uzodimma, accompanied by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr Kingsley Tochukwu Udeh.
According to ALGON, Uzodimma reaffirmed the federal government’s commitment to strengthening grassroots governance, describing effective local government administration as essential to translating government policies into tangible benefits for citizens.
He also expressed support for local government autonomy, institutional strengthening and fiscal viability, saying President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda was designed to extend to the third tier of government.
In response, Lawal expressed appreciation to Tinubu, through Uzodimma, for his commitment to repositioning the local government system. He pledged that ALGON would align its reforms and activities with the administration’s vision across the country’s 774 local government areas and area councils.
The deputy national president of ALGON, Ikenna Adikibe, who chairs the Constitution Amendments Planning Committee and the General Assembly Planning Committee, commended Uzodimma for his leadership and commitment to grassroots development.
Adikibe, who is also the executive chairman of Oru Local Government Area and ALGON chairman in Imo State, described the governor’s visit as a turning point in the assembly.
The meeting was also attended by Hon. Mohammed Abubakar, who was previously associated with a faction of ALGON. The association said his attendance reinforced its position that the years of division affecting its public image were coming to an end.
